items.title: Herb Morand Interview, 1950-03-12
items.q: So, Chris Kelly decided to use me. Well, I was playing second

ctx.x: Well, to sort of summarize this, or to end this, Herb, what were some of your most unusual experiences that you had in your career as a musician playing jazz? Well, I'll tell you,

when I came back from New York, Chris Kelly, I had a whole lot of music and I used to send him music. So, when I came back, they decided, at that time, they were starting to use two trumpets in the jazz band. So, Chris Kelly decided to use me. Well, I was playing second and most of the time, Chris Kelly would be having this fun walking around and talking with the ladies. Well, I'd be playing then. I'd let him play and I'd walk around. So, we had a ballet who were advertising one day and we happened to meet Rene.…

Yeah. And he was also responsible for influencing quite a few of your clarinets, Bechet and musicians such as him. Yeah. He was a great clarinet man. He just about certainly don't recognize clarinet as a clarinet. Yeah, he was in the Orleans. Yeah. But he just have typified the Orleans, New Orleans jazz. Yeah, yeah.
